summary:
We developed a medical telemetry system capable of displaying the crew´s health status through the duration of the mission, addressing and advising the space crew in various health compromising situations and conditions that they might face and keeping a record log after every mission available for its download and for research.

It is meant to be easy to read and comprehension, enabling astronauts to evaluate and act on the status of their health without needing a medical specialization of any sort. By being by themselves in space missions with durations from 1 month to a few months and even years, astronauts could find themselves in situations where their health and wellbeing is compromised and without a medical assistance available to the full extent, this resource is important for them to act on behalf of them and their crew member´s health and safety to ensure their return, as well as keep on research and investigating the more and unique ways the human body reacts to the space environment and how to act about them.
details:
Its works based on a medical telemetry system displaying data such as bpm, oxigenization, exposure to space radiation, blood pressure, hydration and so on, showing them on a main screen for each crew member and keeping record of each reading of this parameters. In case of any situation, a triage of questions is showed for the crewmember to fill in order to know their status, and following this there is a option selection for the various risks, situations or scenarios that an astronaut might face during spaceflight.

We intend for this to help astronauts evaluate and act on behalf of their health status. By keeping in track the health data by every day for the duration of the mission, we intend for this record to help on the research efforts to ensure on better ways to keep the health and wellbeing of the astronauts for their safe return home.

Working on the coding language of Python we developed the whole code and run it using the GitHub website for the its visualization.

Although their creativity may be place in doubt, our main intent is in a easy to understand and comprehend for the astronaut´s decision making and acting, using a color palette where we make sure each status is being noticed regardless.

We consider on top of a everything for this to be practical, comprehendable and understandable for astronauts not only for a daily checking but most importantly for a health consult or a difficult medical situation that requires a quick response. By using easy and redactable steps for the various risks they may face, we ensured that this can be followed and put into practice when needed.
